artworks.title: Alexander the Great Cutting the Gordian Knot
artworks.description: Panini's Walters Art Museum canvas stages Alexander before an altar of Zeus as he slices the yoke-knot on Gordius' wagon at Gordium — the oracle that whoever loosed it would rule Asia. Baroque architecture frames the Phrygian founder's riddle as a single sword-stroke.

artworks.title: Alexander Cutting the Gordian Knot
artworks.description: Altomonte's Baroque history painting packs soldiers and priests around the chariot as Alexander raises his blade over Gordius' inextricable knot. The Phrygian king's wagon — and the prophecy tied to it — become the stage for decisive force.

artworks.title: Alexander Cutting the Gordian Knot
artworks.description: Castaigne's illustration for popular Alexander biographies freezes the cut: the Macedonian king, the ox-cart of Gordius, and the knot that English still calls 'Gordian.' Late-Victorian book art carried Phrygia's founder into classroom and parlour.

popCulture.title: Gordian knot
popCulture.description: From Gordius' wagon-yoke at Gordium to a proverb for any problem solved by cutting rather than untying — the Phrygian king's knot outlived his dynasty.

popCulture.title: Gordias
popCulture.description: Father of Midas and legendary founder of Gordium — remembered less for his reign than for the oracle-knot Alexander cut.
